properties.name: An edge whose prose outlived the node it points at is named by the propagation that surfaces it
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-08-31, on `fact:edge-prose-is-as-perishable-as-node-prose-and-nothing-reads-it`. bhome narrowed a climate requirement and left five RISKS edges still arguing about the arctic; four were repaired only because "the propagation happened to list them and I happened to remember what they said."

THE ASYMMETRY WAS THE FINDING: node prose is governed three ways — an overwrite warning on every `add_*`, `reconcile_artifacts` for design-vs-file drift, `change_axis_unstated` for an unstated axis — and edge prose had none of the three, though an edge property is a claim about the world in exactly the way a node property is.

🛑 IT IS A WARNING AND NEVER A REFUSAL, deliberately. The same surface has just measured what a mis-tuned heuristic guard costs: 15 near-match refusals, zero true positives, and agents who learned to pre-empt it. A warning that names its own crudeness costs a glance; a refusal costs a round trip and teaches the caller to route around it.

Pinned by four tests. The counterweight matters more than the positive one and asserts BOTH that a still-supported edge is not reported AND that the check actually examined it (`edges_with_prose == 1`) — a silent result over an unexamined edge would prove nothing, which is this design's own standing rule about a zero.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
New `crates/reflow2-core/src/edge_prose.rs`: `DesignGraph::stale_edge_evidence(node_id)` returns an `EdgeProseReport` naming incident edges whose `evidence` or `note` still uses language the node has DROPPED, with the specific terms. Wired into `propagate_change`, keyed by seed, so it reaches the reader at the moment they are already looking at those edges.

⭐ IT COMPARES AGAINST THE NODE'S PRIOR STATE, NOT ONLY ITS CURRENT TEXT, and that is the whole design. The obvious version — flag any significant term absent from the node — was written first and REJECTED because it fires on healthy edges: on the reporter's own counter-example, an edge whose evidence still holds contains "demand" and "envelope", neither of which was ever in the requirement. The sharper signal is a term the edge still uses that the node USED TO say and no longer does, which `record_change`'s snapshot already preserves.

`EdgeProseReport` carries `edges_with_prose` (an empty result over zero examined edges is a different fact from one over twenty), a `coverage_note` present ONLY when there is no prior state — saying the check was SILENT about the edges rather than clean on them — and a `caveat` carried with every answer rather than left in the docs where a reader quoting the result would not see it.
